To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pressure and speed of sound of QCD with physical quark mass are well described by a Taylor expansion in μ2 up to the highest chemical potential that we have considered, which is 0.6 times the critical temperature.

(i) the speed of sound is significantly smaller at nonzero chemical potential than at zero chemical potential, (ii) the speed of sounds at nonzero chemical potential is smaller than that of a free gas of pions at the same temperature and chemical potential, (iii) the speed of the sound decreases with increasing chemical potential, (iv) the pressure is negative at low temperatures and small chemical potentials, (v) the entropy density is negative at low temperature and small chemical potentials.
the equation of state at zero chemical potential is very well described by the Taylor expansion up to μ = 400 MeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero chemical potential.
the equation of state at finite temperature and chemical potential.
the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero chemical potential, with the goal of providing a parameterization of the equation of state that can be used for the analysis of heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the QCD equation of state for nonzero chemical potentials is well understood at present, and the Taylor expansion of the equation of state can be reliably used to describe the QCD equation state in the region of the phase diagram accessible in the current generation of relativistic heavy-ion collision experiments.
the equation of state at finite density is well understood at least up to μ ≈ 0.8 T.

the equation of state is in very good agreement with the hadron resonance gas model at low temperature and chemical potential, but shows significant deviations at higher temperatures and chemical potentials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have computed the QCD equation of state in the region of small μ and T, where it is most relevant for the study of the QCD critical point, for the first time using physical masses.

we have computed the equation of state for physical QCD with Nf =2+1 quark flavors at nonzero chemical potential, with the quark mass values corresponding to physical pion mass, and with the strange quark mass set to its physical value, on a variety of lattice spacings and lattice volumes, and that the results are in good agreement with the predictions of the hadron resonance gas model in the low temperature regime.

we have determined the QCD equation of state with physical quark mass at nonzero chemical potential up to O(μ2), and we have provided a parameterization of the observables as a function of temperature, density and entropy density, which can be used for phenomenological applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now compute observables of QCD at nonzero chemical potential with the same accuracy as in the zero chemical potential limit.
the equation of state at small μ is very close to that at μ = 0, even at temperatures close to the transition temperature, where the equation of state is strongly modified.
, at nonzero temperature and density, the equation of state is well described by a Taylor series in μ2.
